core_obligations: Derive one implication (stalks of a flat module are flat) from lemma-stalk-flat (proof lines 7576-7577).

For the converse, record the identity (\mathcal{F} \otimes_\mathcal{O} \mathcal{G})_p = \mathcal{F}_p \otimes_{\mathcal{O}_p} \mathcal{G}_p, because taking stalks at p is given by p^{-1}, via lemma-tensor-product-pullback (proof lines 7578-7582).

Conclude using lemma-check-exactness-stalks that exactness of \mathcal{F} \otimes - is checked on the conservative family of stalks, so \mathcal{F} is flat iff every \mathcal{F}_{p_i} is flat over \mathcal{O}_{p_i} (proof lines 7582-7586).
proof_roadmap: Take the forward direction from the stalk-flat lemma.
Use the stalk-tensor identity to move tensoring with \mathcal{F} past taking stalks.
Apply the conservative-family exactness criterion to conclude.
difficulty_reason: The proof has two halves: the forward implication is the same-chapter lemma that stalks of flat modules are flat (lemma-stalk-flat); for the converse it combines the identity (\mathcal{F} \otimes \mathcal{G})_p = \mathcal{F}_p \otimes_{\mathcal{O}_p} \mathcal{G}_p (stalks commute with tensor, via p^{-1}) with the lemma that exactness is checked on stalks for a conservative family of points, so that exactness of \mathcal{F} \otimes - is detected at every stalk, where it is exactly flatness of \mathcal{F}_p. The transport of flatness through the stalk-tensor identity is the substance.
